changes.before: Active as of 2026-09-23; one-year moratorium on data-center business licenses approved 2026-09-08. Mayor says listening sessions and town halls will follow.

changes.before: None; no proposal pending (several vacant buildings could suit a small data center, per the mayor).
changes.after: As of September 8, 2026, Mayor Threadford said no potential data center developers had approached the city and noted that several buildings for sale could suit a smaller project. Whether any project was proposed or affected remains unverified.

changes.before: One-year moratorium adopted; feasibility study underway.
changes.after: A one-year moratorium was reported approved; city leaders said they wanted to conduct a feasibility study. Whether the study was underway remains unverified.

changes.before: Active as of 2026-09-23 per local reporting; six-month moratorium approved unanimously 2026-08-18. The Planning Commission is researching zoning changes.
changes.after: The council minutes record unanimous approval of a six-month data-center moratorium resolution on August 18, 2026. ABC reported that the Planning Commission planned to research potential zoning changes over the following weeks. Recorded active as of September 23, 2026 in the legacy inventory; that as-of claim and subsequent legal force are unverified.

changes.before: 2026-08-11 (Board of Supervisors adopted an addendum-item resolution at its regular meeting, 3-2 vote)

120 days from adoption (2026-08-11 to approximately 2026-12-09), to give county staff time to finalize a zoning code text amendment establishing data-center-specific regulations; Supervisor Heinz's floor amendment provided the moratorium could return to the board for possible extension before the 120-day limit.
changes.after: A 120-day moratorium was proposed in the August 11, 2026 direction to draft; an adopted term, effective date, expiration and any extension remain unverified. The earlier inventory recorded a possible extension amendment as a historical lead.

changes.before: Resolution adopted by the Pima County Board of Supervisors at its August 11, 2026 regular meeting, added as an addendum item at the request of Board Chair Jennifer Allen (District 3); no separately reported resolution number located in captured sources.
changes.after: Pima County Board of Supervisors File ID 20637: August 11, 2026 addendum directing staff to develop a resolution. Adoption, operative resolution number and later action remain unverified.

changes.before: Pima County Development Services was already drafting a data-center zoning code text amendment (process initiated by a September 2025 BOS vote) when a second, undisclosed data-center project ('Project Gravel,' an 8-building, 160-acre facility near Sahuarita) surfaced via a public-records request; the moratorium bars new data center permit applications while the code amendment is finalized, and (as amended) applies to facilities that have not yet submitted a permit application, so it does not affect the previously permitted 'Project Blue' facility.
changes.after: The county file says the zoning code change process was initiated by a September 2025 Board vote. The legacy inventory associated the proposed moratorium with Project Gravel and described permit effects on Gravel and Project Blue; those project and applicability claims remain unverified historical leads pending source and operative-text review.

changes.before: Active as of 2026-09-23. 120-day moratorium on the acceptance/issuance of new data center permits in unincorporated Pima County, adopted 3-2 (Supervisors Christy and Scott dissenting) on 2026-08-11 and running to approximately 2026-12-09, while Development Services finalizes a zoning code text amendment. The department is seeking public comment (online survey; a September 28, 2026 open house; proposed rules going to the Planning and Zoning Commission on October 28, 2026) on a related, permanent zoning code amendment that would define data centers (facilities using more than 20 MW), require closed-loop cooling, and set review/design standards; that permanent amendment is expected in December 2026, around when the moratorium runs out.
changes.after: On August 11, 2026 the board directed staff to develop a proposed 120-day data-center moratorium; contemporaneous reporting describes a 3–2 vote with Christy and Scott dissenting. A later linked news headline reports a moratorium, but the linked article was not retrieved in the original capped run; adoption, operative scope, duration, later action and present force remain unverified. Recorded active as of September 23, 2026 in the legacy inventory; the as-of claim and related public-comment and zoning-amendment schedule remain unverified historical leads. changes.before: 'Project Gravel,' an undisclosed, 8-building/160-acre data center proposal on land known as Kerley Industrial Park, west of Sahuarita town limits; county officials confirmed the moratorium (as amended to cover unsubmitted permits) would affect this project but not the previously permitted 'Project Blue' data center near the Pima County Fairgrounds.
changes.after: The legacy inventory identified Project Gravel as an 8-building, 160-acre proposal near Sahuarita and claimed it was affected while Project Blue was exempt. These are unverified historical leads; operative provisions and project applicability remain unestablished.

changes.before: Board of Supervisors adopted a 120-day moratorium on new data center permit applications in unincorporated Pima County while the county finalizes a data-center zoning code amendment.
changes.after: On August 11, 2026 the board directed staff to develop a proposed moratorium while county zoning work proceeded; subsequent adoption and operative terms remain unverified.

changes.before: Immediate pause on high-impact industrial and high-intensity digital infrastructure facilities (reported by contemporary coverage to include data centers, artificial intelligence computing facilities, and cryptocurrency mining facilities) in unincorporated Carroll County while the county develops a permitting and public-notice framework
changes.after: Emergency Ordinance 2026-17 temporarily restricts specified construction and county approvals for high-impact industrial and high-intensity digital infrastructure in unincorporated Carroll County while the county develops a permitting and public-notice framework. Article 4 describes qualifying facilities by activity and demand thresholds; Article 9 provides non-retroactivity for specified projects.

changes.before: Active as of 2026-09-23. Adopted 2026-08-10 by unanimous vote under an emergency clause; runs through 2031-08-31, or until the Quorum Court determines a path forward and adopts applicable rules and regulations. No specific data center project had been proposed in the county at adoption.
changes.after: White River Now reported that the Quorum Court passed a five-year commercial data center moratorium on August 10, 2026, with a reported end date of August 31, 2031 and study of future rules. The legacy record reports a unanimous vote, an emergency clause, an earlier rulemaking condition, and no project proposed at adoption; those details remain unverified in the retained bodies reviewed here.
